title: Poached Pear and Chocolate Almond Tart
changes_from_base: Poached pear slices baked under a chocolate and ground almond batter, instead of a plain baked chocolate custard.
summary: Tender poached pears baked into a chocolate and almond filling in a crisp pastry case.

ingredients.item: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
fine sea salt or table salt
ripe but firm pears, peeled, halved and cored

ingredients.note: check the label for milk and soya

steps.title: Pastry
steps.text: rub the flour, icing sugar, salt and butter to crumbs, then mix in the yolk and iced water until it holds. Chill the wrapped disc 30 min, roll it out, line the tin and freeze 20 min.

steps.title: Blind bake
steps.text: heat the oven to 190 °C (170 °C fan). Bake with paper and beans for 20 min, then 8 min uncovered until dry and pale gold. Turn the oven down to 180 °C (160 °C fan).

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: put the water and lemon juice in the saucepan and add each pear half as you prepare it. Add the 100 g sugar, bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 10 min, until just tender. Drain well on kitchen paper. The pears should yield to a knife but still hold their shape.

steps.title: Chocolate mix
steps.text: melt the chocolate over hot water or in short microwave bursts. Beat in the butter in pieces, then the eggs one at a time. Stir in 40 g of the ground almonds with the flour and the 50 g sugar.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: scatter the remaining 20 g almonds over the pastry. Slice each pear half into 4 and lay the slices close together, then spread the chocolate mixture over and between them. Draining the pears well keeps the pastry from going soggy.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: bake 30 min, until the filling has puffed and set. Serve warm or at room temperature, with softly whipped cream if you like.

tips: Keep the poaching syrup to sweeten fruit salads or drinks.
Williams or Comice pears that are just ripe poach evenly.
Fan the slices slightly so each wedge gets some pear.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep covered at room temperature for up to 1 day, or in the fridge for 3 days. Warm slices gently before serving.
